nominations.abstract: Wireless foundation models (WFMs) seek to unify diverse wireless tasks and scenarios, yet existing methods still rely on task- or scenario-specific components or deployment-time fine-tuning. This paper presents an all-in-one wireless model (AWM), a WFM that unifies multi-user channel acquisition and localization, despite their distinct data modalities and functional objectives. We reveal that user location and channel state information (CSI) at different frequencies can be viewed as attribute-specific measurements of the same wireless link. By introducing in-scenario same-attribute reference pairs as prompts, AWM converts heterogeneous attributes into alignable relativity representations, formulating intra-band channel interpolation, inter-band channel prediction, and wireless localization as unified wireless-state transformations. Further, a multi-task MateFormer is developed to perform source-attribute relativity extraction, cross-attribute relativity alignment, and target-attribute synthesis within a unified architecture, avoiding task-specific output heads or downstream fine-tuning. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of model unification, including substantial gains from cross-task knowledge sharing, seamless generalization to unseen scenarios, and an efficient closed-loop service for mobile users.

nominations.title: Pilot-Based Sensing With OFDM and AFDM: A Resource-Matched Performance Comparison
nominations.authors: Siyi Tang, Yin Xu, Aimin Tang, Dazhi He, Wenjun Zhang
nominations.abstract: As a waveform candidate for next-generation wireless systems, affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) has often been compared with orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) under different configurations, while a systematic comparison of their pilot-based sensing performance remains lacking. This paper establishes a comparison with the same bandwidth, frame duration, pilot energy, and reserved-resource overhead. OFDM-random, OFDM-fixed-comb, and OFDM-shifted-comb pilots are compared with AFDM pilots surrounded by guard resources using aperiodic ambiguity functions without cyclic prefix/chirp-periodic prefix (CP/CPP) and cyclic ambiguity functions with CP/CPP, followed by target detection experiments. The results show that OFDM-fixed-comb exhibits low range sidelobes but periodic range ambiguity peaks, while AFDM and OFDM-shifted-comb effectively suppress zero-Doppler range ambiguities. Within the common unambiguous region, all pilot configurations for both waveforms exhibit similar detection thresholds in strong-target detection, while structured OFDM and AFDM pilot placements outperform OFDM-random in weak-target detection. At high mobility, the AFDM receiver using the discrete affine Fourier transform (DAFT) can resolve integer Doppler beyond the conventional slow-time maximum unambiguous velocity, outperforming the tested conventional OFDM and AFDM receivers at the increased search complexity. These results separate the effects of waveform, pilot placement, and receiver processing, providing a basis for AFDM and OFDM pilot-based sensing design.

nominations.title: Temporal vs Spectral Resolution in CSI Reporting for Wi-Fi ISAC
nominations.authors: Abolfazl Zakeri, Sumit Roy, Nhan Thanh Nguyen, Markku Juntti
nominations.abstract: CSI feedback is fundamental to proposed uses of Wi-Fi sensing such as human activity recognition (HAR); but it also constitutes significant overhead as resources must be allocated away from data communications. Wi-Fi CSI extraction can be explored along two dimensions in IEEE 802.11bf: reporting intensity, i.e., temporal resolution, and number of reported subcarriers, i.e., spectral resolution. We explore periodic and IEEE 802.11bf threshold-based reporting at matched rates, and uniform decimation and block-mean grouping at matched report sizes. We further propose reporting the mean CSI accumulated since the last report. Using the 802.11bf report size as the metric, we evaluate the accuracy-cost tradeoffs on three public datasets with our proposed model, a convolutional neural network combined with a gated recurrent unit and temporal pyramid pooling. The proposed periodic reporting with mean payload and block-mean grouping improves accuracy by up to 53 percentage points at equal CSI overhead cost. Temporal resolution is generally more cost-effective than spectral resolution. With only at most 7.7% of full-CSI feedback cost, the proposed scheme achieves 96-98% of full-CSI accuracy.

nominations.title: Sensing-Driven Secure Transmission with Mobile Eavesdropper Tracking in RIS-Assisted ISAC
nominations.authors: Jie Li, Ning Wang, Zhendong Li, Ze Li, Lingfeng Shen, Zhongyun Li, Jiakang Zheng
nominations.abstract: The mobility of potential eavesdroppers (Eves) poses a critical challenge to physical-layer security (PLS) in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, since rapidly varying Eve positions lead to time-varying eavesdropping channels and outdated security decisions. To address this challenge, this paper investigates sensing-driven secure transmission for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted ISAC systems with a maneuvering Eve. To this end, by exploiting the dual functionality of the ISAC waveform, a multi-view angle estimation method jointly exploiting the base station (BS) and RIS is developed based on MUSIC and maximum likelihood estimation (MLE), enabling three-dimensional (3D) Eve localization, whose accuracy is characterized by the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB). Subsequently, an interacting multiple model extended Kalman filter (IMM-EKF) with out-of-sequence measurement (OOSM) compensation is employed to track and predict the maneuvering Eve. Based on the predicted trajectory, the time-varying eavesdropping channel is updated, and the transmit beamforming and RIS phase shifts are jointly optimized subject to a sensing CRLB constraint. Furthermore, an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm integrating fractional programming, semidefinite relaxation (SDR), and Riemannian manifold optimization is developed to solve the resulting non-convex problem. Finally, numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately tracking maneuvering Eves and enhancing secure transmission in dynamic ISAC environments.

nominations.title: A Smaller Subspace is All You Need: Efficient ISAC Beamforming via Dimensionality Reduction
nominations.authors: Ruiqi Liu, Yuanshuo Gang, Tianqi Mao, Qingqing Wu
nominations.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has been recognized as a critical technology for the sixth generation (6G) wireless networks. Under monostatic sensing mode, achieving a balance between communication and sensing performance via optimal beamforming is a critical research problem. In multiple input multiple output (MIMO) systems, such beamforming problems are of substantial computational complexity due to the large number of antennas. Existing methods exploit exact subspaces of lower dimensions to speed up the beamforming process where the complexity is proportional to the number of communication users and sensing targets instead of antennas. In this paper, it is demonstrated that the beamforming problem can be solved in an even lower-dimensional subspace with only a small sensing performance loss. Numerical results compare the sensing performance and computational complexity of ISAC beamforming problem in the exact subspace and smaller subspaces.

nominations.title: Beyond Latent Personalization: Integrating HRV-Conditioned Personalization via LLM for Interpretable Stress Detection
nominations.authors: Wei-Hsiang Ma, Ya-Tse Wu, Hsing-Hang Chou, Chi-Chun Lee
nominations.abstract: Stress detection based on heart rate variability (HRV) has received increasing attention. However, existing personalized approaches integrate personal attributes with HRV through latent representations, limiting the interpretability of their interactions. In this work, we propose an LLM-enhanced personalized stress detection framework that integrates HRV features and personal attributes through LLM-based semantic interpretation. The proposed framework achieves a 29.9% relative MCC improvement over the strongest baseline on TILES-2018 while providing human-readable descriptions of individual physiological responses. The results highlight the potential of LLM-based semantic interpretation for achieving both effective and interpretable personalized stress detection.

nominations.title: Packet Loss Analysis Under Doppler Effects and Reinforcement-Learning-Based Resource Allocation for Direct-to-Satellite LoRaWAN
nominations.authors: Alireza Maleki, Ebrahim Bedeer, Robert Barton
nominations.abstract: Long range wide area network (LoRaWAN) has a long communication range and low power consumption, making it a potential technology for direct-to-satellite (DtS) Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity. However, packet collisions and Doppler impairments brought on by satellite motion can greatly increase the packet loss ratio (PLR) in large-scale DtS-IoT networks. In this paper, we study resource allocation in DtSIoT LoRaWAN by first developing an analytical PLR model that simultaneously takes Doppler impairments and packet collisions in the temporal and frequency domains into account. In order to maximize resource allocation, the generated PLR is then used as the reward function for two reinforcement learning (RL) schemes: deep Q-network (DQN) and proximal policy optimization (PPO). Simulation results validate the analytical PLR model against Monte Carlo simulations and demonstrate significant improvements over random resource allocation. At a target PLR of 3*10^-2, while random allocation supports only 100 end devices (EDs), PPO and DQN support approximately 650 and 690 EDs, respectively, representing nearly a seven-fold increase. Furthermore, for 800 EDs, PPO and DQN increase the total number of transmitted packets by 106.7% and 88.0%, respectively, compared with random allocation.

nominations.title: Typical Superpositions are Magical
nominations.authors: Joshuah T. Heath, Andrew Urilyon, Damien Quinn, Graham Kells
nominations.abstract: The non-stabilizerness, or "magic", of a quantum state is a common metric for the hardness of simulation on a classical computer, and is often quantified by the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy (SRE). We show how random superpositions of classically simulable states saturate the SRE to the symmetry-restricted Haar-random maximum. For any large-$N$ random pure-state ensemble satisfying the conditions of Schur's lemma, the average SRE of the $m$-component superposition $\langle M_2(m)\rangle=N-\log_2[\langle W(m)\rangle]$ is governed by an average witness $\langle W(m)\rangle$ that universally decomposes into a Haar floor and an ensemble-specific excess. As the number of components $m$ increases, the excess is suppressed, resulting in a logarithmic scaling of the SRE before plateauing at the Haar-valued maximum. We derive a general closed form for $\langle W(m)\rangle$ in the thermodynamic limit, and numerically verify our result for random stabilizer states and random Gaussian states.

nominations.title: Exploring Quantum Phase Transitions Beyond Landau Theory on a Quantum Processor
nominations.authors: Ruizhe Shen, Yin Zhong, Ching Hua Lee
nominations.abstract: Direct continuous quantum phase transitions between phases that break distinct symmetries challenge the conventional Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm and provide a framework for deconfined quantum criticality. Here, we investigate a Landau-forbidden ferromagnetic-to-valence-bond-solid (FM-VBS) transition in a frustrated one-dimensional spin chain using superconducting quantum processors. Combining matrix-product-state-assisted circuit preparation with quantum-hardware measurements, we resolve the suppression of long-range ferromagnetic correlations and the redistribution of competing-order fluctuations across the transition. Distance-resolved correlations and finite-size analyses reveal signatures consistent with critical behavior. We further extend our investigation to nonequilibrium dynamics, directly preparing dimerized states and tracking the evolution of VBS order and joint FM-VBS fluctuations under local unitary interactions. Our results establish a versatile quantum-hardware framework for probing competing orders, critical correlations, and many-body dynamics beyond conventional Landau theory.

nominations.title: Multi-Time States in Quantum and Operational Probabilistic Theories: An Axiomatic Framework
nominations.authors: Kaumudibikash Goswami, Archana Barvar, Manabendra Nath Bera
nominations.abstract: Quantum states over time were introduced, in part, to extend Bayesian probability to quantum theory and have since found applications across diverse areas, ranging from quantum causality and open-system dynamics to tests of macroscopic realism. While axiomatic characterizations of these states exist for Markovian dynamics, a general framework accommodating non-Markovian dynamics is still lacking. Moreover, extending this framework beyond quantum mechanics to general physical theories also remains elusive. In this work, we develop an axiomatic framework for multi-time states within a class of operational probabilistic theories (OPTs) that includes quantum mechanics as a special case. Based on three assumptions---compositionality, reconstructibility, and spatio-temporal marginal consistency---the framework accommodates both Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics, and provides sufficient conditions to certify signaling and temporal memory within OPT. As a concrete application of our OPT framework, we fully characterize the unique multi-time state in boxworld and develop a method for Bayesian retrodiction of physical transformations there. Our general framework is consistent with quantum theory, reproducing several existing results. In the non-Markovian quantum dynamics, we establish a correspondence between multi-time states and the process-matrix framework, and fully characterize the multi-time states compatible with general dynamics. This correspondence also lets us infer quantum causal models from multi-time states, and as a proof of principle, we propose a semidefinite program to infer causal order from quantum multi-time states. These results provide a unified framework for studying spatio-temporal states, causal relations, and Bayesian reasoning within OPTs, with implications for both fundamental and applied research.

nominations.title: Resonant pair production and flat band melting in a driven Rydberg chain
nominations.authors: Tista Banerjee, K. Sengupta
nominations.abstract: We study a Rydberg chain subjected to a two-tone periodic drive of the detuning $\Delta(t)$ and Rabi frequency $\Omega(t)$ at frequencies $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2=\nu \omega_1$ respectively with $\nu \in \mathbf{Z}$. In the strong Rydberg blockade limit, such a system reduces to the PXP model and exhibits exact Floquet flat band. Here we determine, using a time-dependent Schrieffer-Wolff transformation, the domain of validity of such PXP dynamics once the blockade-violating processes are taken into account. We study the melting of such flat bands in the presence of strong, but finite, blockade strength. Using Floquet perturbation theory (FPT), we identify two mechanisms for such melting; the first occurs due to the presence of many-body resonances involving resonant production of nearest-neighbor Rydberg excitation pairs while the second involves virtual processes that access intermediate states with such pairs. Our analytical FPT results match with those obtained using exact diagonalization on a finite chain. We study the dynamics for $|{\rm vac}\rangle$ (Fock state with no Rydberg excitation), $|{\mathbb {Z}}_2\rangle$, and $|{\mathbb {Z}}_3\rangle$ (Fock states with Rydberg excitations on alternate and every third site respectively) initial states. We find that $|{\rm vac}\rangle$ shows exceptional stability against resonant pair formation while $|{\mathbb {Z}}_3\rangle$ exhibits flat band melting via virtual processes away from the direct resonances. We find oscillatory dynamics with large time period for the $|{\mathbb {Z}}_2\rangle$ initial state and the presence of Floquet scars that have large overlap with $|{\mathbb {Z}}_3\rangle$ state; these phenomena occur due to processes that are absent in the PXP limit. We propose measurement of nearest neighbor pair correlation functions using Rydberg atom quantum simulator platforms as an accessible experimental probe for these effects.

nominations.title: A thermally and perturbatively stable classical spin model in two dimensions
nominations.authors: Shankar Balasubramanian, Margarita Davydova, Ting-Chun Lin, Ryan Thorngren
nominations.abstract: We show that the 2D classical spin model constructed in arXiv:2605.10943 hosts many metastable states at non-zero temperature which are stable to arbitrary Hamiltonian perturbations, providing the first such example. Our proof relies on a recursive application of the cluster expansion.

nominations.title: Circuit Synthesis for Variational Quantum Algorithms: The Depth of Algebra and Geometry
nominations.authors: Boris Tsvelikhovskiy
nominations.abstract: The analysis of Hamiltonian Variational Ans\"atze centers on three fundamental questions: which states are exactly reachable from a given initial state, what native control depth suffices for local and global synthesis, and whether a bounded circuit extension can expose a direction of decreasing cost at a suboptimal output. We address these challenges by leveraging the dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) associated with the circuits and the geometry of the initial state's orbit under the action of the corresponding dynamical Lie group $G$. We show that an initial state has a closed projective orbit whenever it is a nondegenerate eigenstate of a control Hamiltonian. Combined with asymptotic QAOA convergence, this guarantees exact, finite depth ground state preparation for architectures employing diagonal problem Hamiltonians and irreducible stoquastic mixers. We bound the number of native control exponentials required for local unitary synthesis and state preparation using DLA commutator filtration growth alongside reachable orbit dimensions. Complementing these local results, we construct global frameworks on invariant sectors equipped with full unitary or special unitary dynamical Lie algebras. These constructions yield explicit applications to Pauli-generated systems and constrained maximum independent set multi-angle QAOA circuits; specifically, we show that their native control costs are directly determined by commutator filtration depth and independent-set toggle-group geometry, respectively. Finally, if the dynamical Lie group is compact, the observable $H_P$ generates an admissible evolution ($iH_P \in \mathfrak{g}$, where $\mathfrak{g}$ is the DLA), and the projective orbit of the initial state contains a ground state ray of $H_P$, then a bounded depth, identity-initialized circuit extension exhibits either first-order descent or negative curvature at every suboptimal circuit output.

nominations.title: Quantum-Classical Neural Networks for Solving Lindblad Master Equations
nominations.authors: Rafael Florencio D\'iaz, Julio Guerrero Garc\'ia, Elvira Romera Guti\'errez
nominations.abstract: Variational quantum algorithms have emerged as a promising approach for simulating open quantum systems, yet their expressive power and trainability remain poorly understood. We propose a variational framework for solving Lindblad master equations by minimizing a residual cost function using a compositional ansatz obtained by combining a classical neural network with a parameterized quantum circuit. The density matrix is represented through a purification on an enlarged Hilbert space, ensuring positivity, Hermiticity, and unit trace by construction, while all gradients are evaluated exactly via the parameter-shift rule. Beyond the algorithmic formulation, we derive an upper bound for the covering number of the proposed compositional model and compare it with that of purely quantum neural networks. Our analysis shows that the classical parametrization enlarges the effective hypothesis class while providing finer control over its complexity, thereby establishing a theoretical connection between expressivity, covering numbers, effective dimension, and the barren plateau phenomenon. Numerical experiments validate both the accuracy of the proposed method for representative Lindblad master equations and the theoretical predictions regarding gradient concentration. These results provide a unified variational and theoretical framework for the simulation of dissipative quantum dynamics using compositional quantum machine learning models.

nominations.title: Metric and Dispersive Dynamics of Phase Perturbations in Bohmian Quantum Mechanics
nominations.authors: Felipe S. Esc\'orcio, Hermano Velten
nominations.abstract: By linearizing the hydrodynamic equations associated with the Madelung transformation in the context of Bohmian dynamics, we derive an effective metric for the phase perturbation around a background state. We show that the metric previously obtained previously by the same authors arises naturally as a particular case of a more general structure, in which the complete functional variation of the quantum potential is retained and external classical potentials can be incorporated. This generalization preserves the dependence of the quantum potential on the density and its spatial derivatives, generating additional terms that introduce dispersive corrections and act as sources in the effective Klein-Gordon equation. To organize these contributions, we introduce differential operators that separate the local sector responsible for the effective geometry from the corrections associated with the complete functional structure of the quantum potential. We identify the conditions under which these additional terms become negligible, recovering homogeneous propagation and the effective geometry for the Gaussian wave packet of a free particle.

nominations.title: Programmable Preparation of Topological Entangled States
nominations.authors: M. Javad Zakeri, Alaric Pan, Darren D Hudson, Andrea Blanco-Redondo
nominations.abstract: Programmable preparation of entangled quantum states is a central requirement for scalable quantum information processing, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing. Topological photonic platforms offer an attractive route towards robust quantum-state generation by encoding information in symmetry- protected optical modes, yet the generated entangled states are typically dictated by the lattice geometry and therefore lack programmability. Here we demonstrate programmable preparation of topological entangled states by inverse engineering the nonlinear optical pump profile of an integrated photonic lattice. Our approach enables deterministic control over both the dimensionality and modal structure of the generated entangled state while preserving its topological character. We experimentally realize silicon photonic topological superlattices in which the nonlinear generation pathway itself becomes programmable via tailored excitations. The superlattices host a multiband manifold of co localized topological interface modes, while coherently controlled inputs synthesize pump superpositions within this protected basis. We showcase this principle by selectively addressing topological biphoton eigenstates, steering correlations to produce a desired target state in a high-dimensional Hilbert space, and inverse-designing pump states that generate targeted Schmidt dimensionalities. Site-resolved two-photon correlation measurements remain reproducible across nominally identical fabricated devices, demonstrating robustness to realistic nanofabrication-induced disorder. Programmable preparation of topological entangled states establishes a pathway towards exploiting topological photonic modes as application-specific quantum resources, enabling tailored input states for high-dimensional quantum communication, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing.

nominations.title: The Classical Boundary of Quantum Computation: History-Resolved Causal Stochastic Machines and the Cost of Classicalization
nominations.authors: Kyoungho Cho, Junghee Ryu, Minsu Kim, Jeongho Bang
nominations.abstract: What separates quantum computation from classical computation when a classical model may retain every branch history and arbitrary causal memory? We study this question using history-resolved causal stochastic machines (HCSMs), which describe positive causal history laws. Probabilistic Turing machines (PTMs) embed in stochastic-ensemble models (SEnMs), which in turn embed in HCSMs. We prove that HCSM history laws coincide exactly with the fixed-basis, prefix-preserving diagonal sector of ideal quantum processes, denoted by $\mathsf{PTM}_{\rm proc}$ and distinguished here from algorithmic quantum Turing machines (QTMs). Coherent quantum processes extend strictly beyond this sector. The boundary is already visible in reversibility. Born-probability shadows of unitary gates preserve inverse composition exactly for basis permutations with phases. Outside this class, an exact positive stochastic simulation that supports universal quantum continuations must retain predictive information absent from visible probabilities. An inverse-recovery identity quantifies this phase ledger, and universal continuation forces the retained probability law to be tomographically sufficient for the quantum state. Under continuous full-state encoding assumptions, this requirement yields quantum-state dimension lower bounds. The familiar slogan $\mathsf{PTM}\subseteq\mathsf{QTM}$ is thereby sharpened into a precise classical boundary and a no-free-classicalization principle. Complete classical branching does not remove the predictive information needed to represent quantum coherence.

nominations.title: Quantumness of Entanglement in Schwarzschild de Sitter Spacetime
nominations.authors: Sumeng Wang, Xiaofen Huang
nominations.abstract: We investigate genuine multipartite entanglement and genuine tripartite nonlocality of a noisy generalized GHZ state in Schwarzschild-de Sitter spacetime. The genuine multipartite concurrence and optimized Svetlichny parameter are employed to characterize these two quantum correlations. It is shown that the black hole and cosmological event horizons redistribute genuine multipartite entanglement differently among the physically accessible and inaccessible reduced states, while Svetlichny violation occurs only in the physically accessible state. We find that genuine multipartite entanglement can survive in the physically inaccessible states even when genuine tripartite nonlocality is absent. In addition, initial white noise suppresses both correlations, with Svetlichny nonlocality surviving over a narrower parameter region. Furthermore, in the Nariai limit, under the normalization adopted here, the correlations become concentrated in the physically accessible state. These results demonstrate the different robustness of genuine multipartite entanglement and genuine tripartite nonlocality under horizon effects and initial noise.

nominations.title: On the relationship between the POVM framework and the no-signaling hypothesis
nominations.authors: Will Cavendish
nominations.abstract: The quantum foundations literature contains dozens of "no-signaling" arguments that rely on the Born rule or, more generally, the positive operator-valued measure (POVM) framework to show that the resources of non-relativistic quantum mechanics (NRQM) cannot be used to send superluminal signals. What these arguments typically establish, however, is not a prohibition on superluminal signaling per se, but the seemingly stronger claim that signaling at any speed between mutually isolated systems is forbidden. This paper gives a precise formulation of this claim, the no-signaling hypothesis, and investigates the following converse question: under what additional assumptions does it imply that all experimental outcome probabilities are described by POVMs? Surprisingly few are needed: given the standard NRQM representation of composite experiments and two textbook claims about marginal probabilities, the no-signaling hypothesis is equivalent to the universality of the POVM framework. More broadly, by formalizing the relevant concepts and deriving the logical relationships between them, the paper shows that the no-signaling hypothesis can be used to derive most, though not all, of the probability-generating fragment of NRQM. The resulting map of implications clarifies which common postulates of NRQM are logically interrelated and which can be modified independently.

nominations.title: Quantum approximate stochastic combinatorial optimisation
nominations.authors: Edric Matwiejew, Paulo E. Santos, Jingbo B. Wang, Ugo Varetto
nominations.abstract: Two-stage stochastic combinatorial optimisation concerns discrete decisions made before all relevant information is known. An initial decision is made; once uncertainty is resolved, it can be adapted to the realised scenario, at a cost. The aim is to find the initial decision that minimises the upfront cost plus the expected cost of optimal adaptation. The first-stage decision problem is often NP-hard, and computing the expected minimum recourse cost can be $\#\mathrm{P}$-hard for a single first-stage candidate. We introduce Quantum Approximate Stochastic Combinatorial Optimisation (QASCO), a variational quantum-walk ansatz that coherently incorporates scenario-dependent recourse into its dynamics to search over first-stage decisions without explicitly evaluating expected minimum recourse costs. We demonstrate QASCO for MaxCut with stochastic edge weights, obtain a circuit with polynomial per-layer gate complexity, and study the ansatz via exact state-vector simulation. Across the instances considered, QASCO concentrates amplitude more effectively on stochastic-optimal first-stage decisions than a previously proposed two-stage QAOA construction. We further show that the ansatz can be calibrated using a depth-independent number of parameters and applied to unseen instances without further circuit-parameter optimisation, including joint decision--scenario--recourse spaces spanning more than $2^{32}$ configurations. Under a query-cost model, comparison with the tested classical heuristics using sample-average approximations of the expected minimum recourse cost shows that QASCO more reliably reaches globally optimal first-stage solutions while requiring fewer cut evaluations. These results show how to incorporate scenario-dependent recourse into the ansatz dynamics, providing a general framework for variational quantum walks in two-stage stochastic combinatorial optimisation.

nominations.title: Quantum-Assisted Unambiguous Discrimination of Pure States with Robustness Bounds
nominations.authors: Jinhyeok Heo, Dongkeun Lee, Junghee Ryu, Minjin Choi
nominations.abstract: We propose a hybrid quantum-classical framework for the unambiguous discrimination of pure states by combining the noisy intermediate-scale quantum semidefinite program solver (NSS) with the reciprocal-state representation. In NSS, a given semidefinite program (SDP) is represented within a subspace spanned by chosen ansatz states, with the required quantities estimated using quantum circuits, and the resulting optimization is performed classically. This makes NSS naturally applicable to discrimination problems involving circuit-prepared states, as finding a discrimination measurement can be formulated as an SDP. By choosing the discriminated states themselves as the ansatz and exploiting the reciprocal-state representation, the general matrix-variable NSS formulation is reduced to an optimization over N scalar variables, where N is the number of discriminated states. The resulting formulation reduces the number of optimization variables and positive-semidefinite constraints compared with the original NSS formulation. We further establish robustness guarantees against Gram matrix estimation errors, including a rescaling procedure that guarantees a valid positive operator-valued measure (POVM) under bounded perturbations. The resulting bounds quantify both the deviation in average success probability and violations of the no-error condition using only the estimated Gram matrix, its SDP solution, and a characterized perturbation bound, without access to the ideal Gram matrix. Numerical simulations validate the derived robustness bounds and characterize finite-shot scaling. We also perform experiments on IBM quantum hardware to estimate pairwise overlaps, and then evaluate the performance of the resulting POVMs.

nominations.title: Encodings and Node Architecture: Lessons from the Fault-Tolerant Distributed Transversal Fanout
nominations.authors: Seng W. Loke
nominations.abstract: An encoding choice specifies the quantum error-correcting code used to encode logical qubits at a given node. Different encoding choices may differ in the number of physical qubits, the number of encoded logical qubits, the code distance, and the available fault-tolerant operations. We study different encodings for a distributed transversal fanout operation and look at its implications on node architecture. Our experiments suggest that an encoding with higher distance, even if requiring more ebits, can yield a lower logical error rate for distributed operations, and that ``upgrading'' an encoding prior to distributed operations and having a cache, as part of node architecture, for qubits can be useful for distributed operations.

nominations.title: Quantum Tsallis Entropy Estimation: Near-Optimal Bounds and High-Precision Improvements
nominations.authors: Chengshen Gao, Zongxing Xiong, Lvzhou Li
nominations.abstract: Estimating statistical properties of probability distributions is a fundamental problem in statistics and theoretical computer science. We develop quantum algorithms for estimating the $q$-Tsallis entropy $\mathrm{H}_q^{\mathrm{Tsa}}(P) =\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n p_i^q-1}{1-q}$ when $0<q<1$, given purified quantum query access to a distribution $P$ on $[n]$. When $0<q\leq \frac{1}{2}$, we provide a quantum algorithm with query complexity $\widetilde{O}\rbra{\left(\frac{n}{\varepsilon}\right)^{\frac{1}{2q}}}$, which is optimal up to polylogarithmic factors. When $\frac{1}{2}<q<1$, we introduce a two-stage simultaneous probability estimation procedure, yielding a quantum algorithm with query complexity $\widetilde{O}\left(\frac{n^{\frac12+\frac{1}{2q}}}{\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{2q}}}+\frac{n^{1-q}}{\varepsilon}\right)$, which improves the result given by Chen et al. (ICALP 2026) when $\varepsilon=O\rbra{n^{1-2q}}$.

nominations.title: Discrete time crystals and classical logic gates in coupled open Dicke models
nominations.authors: Emmanuel D. G. U, Roy D. Jara Jr., Jayson G. Cosme
nominations.abstract: We investigate the dynamics of coupled discrete time crystals (DTCs) in the coupled Dicke model or Dicke dimer (DD) with dissipation. By numerically simulating the mean-field dynamics of the system, we show that coupling two DTCs decreases their oscillation amplitude following a transient relaxation period. For sufficiently strong coupling, the coupled DTCs become unstable, resulting in the system relaxing towards the normal phase (NP). We demonstrate that the relaxation time diverges near the critical coupling strength, suggesting a continuous phase transition. Using the truncated Wigner approximation (TWA), we explore how the dynamics are affected by the introduction of quantum fluctuations. We also consider a scenario in which an NP is briefly coupled to a DTC, seeding the NP to transform into a DTC that is either synchronized or anti-synchronized relative to the DTC. We investigate the robustness of this phenomenon in the presence of noise. Using these results, we propose a scheme to perform NAND and NOR operations with three DTCs by sequentially coupling the input and output sites. We identify the parameter regimes in which the logic gate architecture remains valid, and investigate how the protocol is affected by the presence of quantum fluctuations.

nominations.title: Concrete Functions in Private Simultaneous Quantum Messages: Quantum Advantages and Structural Limitations
nominations.authors: Harumichi Nishimura
nominations.abstract: Private simultaneous quantum messages (PSQM) provide a minimal model of noninteractive secure multiparty quantum computation, yet their communication complexity for concrete functions remains poorly understood. We show that familiar total functions already exhibit both genuine quantum advantages and strong structural limitations. For three-party equality on $n$-bit inputs, which determines whether the players' $n$-bit strings are identical, we construct an entanglement-assisted protocol with asymptotic communication $(1.633\ldots)n$ qubits, whereas every perfectly correct protocol without prior entanglement requires at least $3n$ qubits. For three-bit majority, one shared GHZ state and one transmitted qubit per player suffice for perfect correctness and perfect privacy, reducing the communication from the optimal classical cost of six bits to three qubits. Three-bit AND behaves differently. No perfectly correct and perfectly private protocol exists when the players share an arbitrary three-qubit state, apply arbitrary local unitary encodings, and transmit one qubit each. However, increasing the local dimension overcomes this obstruction: one shared three-qutrit GHZ state and one transmitted qutrit per player yield a one-shot protocol with total communication $3\log_2 3$. Together with the six-bit classical lower bound, this gives a strict quantum communication advantage. More generally, for every $k\geq 3$, we construct a perfectly correct and perfectly private one-shot protocol for $k$-bit AND using one qudit of dimension at most $k$ per player, and hence at most $k\log_2 k$ qubits in total.

nominations.title: Nonequilibrium Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions in the Extended Agassi Model
nominations.authors: Ritesh Kumar Palai, Rajiv Kumar, Venktesh Singh, Sunil K. Mishra
nominations.abstract: We investigate dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs) in the extended Agassi model following sudden quenches of same level pairing ($\Sigma$), monopole-monopole ($\chi$) and cross level pairing ($\Lambda$) strengths. Using exact diagonalization, we characterize the non-equilibrium dynamics through the Loschmidt echo and intensive return-rate function. Quenches across equilibrium phase boundaries produce cusp-like structures in the return rate that shows non-analyticities with increasing system size. Equilibrium finite size to large scaling identifies the $\chi$-driven transition as a second order phase transition similar to mean-field, Dicke, and Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick (LMG) models critical behaviour with the exponent of the order parameter $\beta \simeq 1/2$, while the $\Sigma$- and $\Lambda$-driven transitions are first order. We further characterize the associated dynamical singularities through a local scaling exponent $\alpha$, with $\alpha_\chi \simeq 2/3$, $\alpha_\Lambda \simeq 1/3$, and $\alpha_\Sigma \simeq 3/2$ of all three parameters. The distinct scaling behaviours across the parameter channels show that dynamical criticality is not determined solely by the equilibrium order of the transition, revealing multiple dynamical scaling regimes. These non-analyticities are associated with the Fisher zeros of the Loschmidt amplitude, which cross the real time axis at critical times and the time derivatives of the return-rate function to characterize the order of DQPTs within the extended Agassi model.

nominations.title: Liouvillian Non-Invertible Symmetry
nominations.authors: Ying-Cheng Yang, Jhen-Dong Lin, Yueh-Nan Chen
nominations.abstract: Non-invertible symmetries extend conventional symmetries beyond group-like transformations and play an important role in quantum field theory and many-body physics. However, a general framework of non-invertible symmetries in open quantum systems is still lacking. Here, we formulate a general Liouville-space duality framework that extends Hilbert-space non-invertible dualities to open quantum systems. The resulting defect relates Liouvillians with dual Hamiltonian and dissipative parameters and becomes an exact symmetry at self-duality. We apply this framework to the periodic transverse-field Ising chain with two collective Lindblad channels exchanged by Kramers--Wannier (KW) duality. A strong $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry divides Liouville space into four parity sectors, while the defect acts nontrivially only in the even-even sector. At self-duality, the KW defect imposes a momentum-resolved selection rule on Liouvillian Jordan blocks. Modes with different Liouville momenta or KW-defect eigenvalues cannot form a common exceptional Jordan block. For a three-site chain, a global R\'enyi-2 KW asymmetry dynamically identifies the self-dual conditions. At the same time, the spectral structure exhibits both a semisimple degeneracy and a self-dual exceptional point with a perturbation-selective response. These results extend non-invertible dualities to Markovian quantum dynamics and establish a symmetry-based selection rule for Liouvillian Jordan structures.

nominations.title: Recoverability-Controlled Safety Miscalibration in Large Language Models
nominations.authors: Yuwei Wang, Xingwang Liang, Yu Xie, Haotian Chi, Haijun Geng
nominations.abstract: Safety-aligned language models are expected to refuse harmful requests while remaining useful for benign ones. However, because many evaluations score only the final response, they often conflate intent understanding with response-level safety behavior. To address this, we introduce RiskCueBench, a recoverability-controlled benchmark that separates these two stages by first measuring whether a model can successfully recover a high-level intent and then evaluating its safety behavior on the same prompt. RiskCueBench contains 160 latent intents and 640 abstract non-operational surface prompts across eight risk categories. The benchmark covers 25 completed model groups and 32,000 successful model outputs with final rubric-adjudicated labels. When conditioning on pairs where both surface forms are recoverable, we find that increased contextualized specificity induces a shift toward less safe behavior. Specifically, paired bootstrap estimates show that the refusal rate and global safety score decrease by 0.175 and 0.440, respectively. Furthermore, mixed effects modeling corroborates a 0.107 increase in unsafe cooperation. These results show that the safety behavior can be miscalibrated to the surface form even after the intent has been recovered, motivating safety evaluations that report response behavior conditional on semantic recoverability.

nominations.title: An Agentic ENF Framework for Forensic Video Authentication Against Generative AI
nominations.authors: Ryan Wyton (Southampton Solent University), Bacha Rehman (Southampton Solent University)
nominations.abstract: Generative models now synthesise video that is hard to distinguish from genuine footage, and learned detectors that key on a generator's artefacts degrade sharply on unseen models. This paper develops a forensic framework that authenticates video by a signal that generation does not control: the electric network frequency (ENF), the mains-driven hum in audio and flicker in video. A unified two-channel detector extracts the ENF from audio and from rolling-shutter video through one second harmonic estimator and a shared network; a synthetic-injection training method, driven by an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck drift model and anchored to real recordings, overcomes the scarcity of labelled ENF data; a reference-matching channel verifies a claimed time of recording and recovers an unknown one; and a two-axis agentic orchestrator fuses recording authenticity with content-manipulation evidence under an asymmetric rule, escalating expensive detectors only when needed. A central finding reframes the task: an ENF-band flicker is present in generated video at a prominence indistinguishable from real footage, so its presence is not proof of authenticity, and authentication must rest on consistency with an independent reference rather than on presence. On held-out real recordings the detector accepts genuine audio and video at 93% and 100% against naive baselines of 53% and 15%; claimed-time authentication reaches an area under the curve of 1.0; and the agentic cascade matches a flat ensemble while cutting wall-clock time by 54% and frames decoded by 64%, without loss of accuracy.

nominations.title: Capital Costs Protect the Network: Mining Gap Dynamics in Proof-of-Work Blockchains Under a Stochastic Mempool
nominations.authors: Hasan Sel\c{c}uk K{\i}l{\i}\c{c}, Nail Akar
nominations.abstract: Proof-of-Work blockchains increasingly rely on transaction fees to keep miners engaged as block subsidies decline. An immediate outcome of this is that miners may sit idle at the start of a round until enough high-fee transactions accumulate in order to make mining worthwhile. This idle period is known as the mining gap. We model the high-fee transaction backlog as a Lindley-type recursion under a two-tier fee market and use its stationary distribution to characterize the mining gap. Under Bitcoin's difficulty-adjustment mechanism, the expected gap grows strictly with the hashpower active on the network and consumes the entire round as that hashpower grows without bound. A free-entry condition determines a unique long-run equilibrium hashpower. Capital cost caps the equilibrium hashpower and prevents the mining gap from occupying the entire round. We further characterize how the block subsidy, transaction fees, and operating cost shape the equilibrium hashpower and the mining gap.

nominations.title: Erase the Mark, Preserve the Motion: Temporally Consistent Removal of Video Watermarks
nominations.authors: Yifan Liao, Zhen Sun, Zhicong Huang, Jiaming He, Zongmin Zhang, Xi Ai, Cheng Hong, Xinhu Zheng, Xinlei He
nominations.abstract: Recent advances in video generation have increased the demand for reliable watermarking for copyright protection, yet the robustness of video watermarks against removal attacks remains underexplored. Most watermark-removal methods originate from the image domain: signal optimization injects imperceptible pixel-domain perturbations, whereas generative resynthesis produces a visually similar instance through diffusion synthesis. When extended to videos, the former introduces temporally varying noise that causes visible flickering, while the latter regenerates fine-grained structures inconsistently across frames, leading to structural motion inconsistency. To evaluate video watermark robustness, we propose PoseRegen, a pose-consistent reconstruction framework that removes watermarks while preserving the original content and motion. PoseRegen first applies a temporally shared viewpoint transformation to disrupt watermark-bearing spatial patterns and then jointly reconstructs the transformed sequence with a pose-conditioned video model. A frozen video DiT processes the complete sequence with its reference-video latent, and full-sequence Flow Matching supervision keeps identity and background consistent across frames. To further preserve motion structure, we introduce a lightweight Pose-Conditioned Motion Consistency Adapter that adapts the frozen backbone to temporally ordered pose guidance and constrains body-part trajectories throughout reconstruction. Experiments on eleven video watermarking schemes show that PoseRegen reduces the average bit accuracy to 0.505, near random guessing, while outperforming the strongest baseline by 9.34% on motion-related VBench metrics. These results reveal a practical vulnerability of current video watermarks and highlight the need to evaluate robustness jointly with temporal and motion quality.

nominations.title: Everyone's a little bit racist: a novel ML backdoor attack in black-box mode
nominations.authors: Michele Cerrta, Gabriele Costa
nominations.abstract: Backdoors are among the most impactful attacks against Machine Learning (ML), yet most existing methods assume some form of training-time poisoning or direct model manipulation. This is often considered sufficient to assume that existing systems are not exposed to actual risks. In this paper, we introduce Backdoor-as-a-Service, a model-agnostic, fully black-box technique that, instead of installing a backdoor, activates it in the form of a latent secondary task leveraging on an already present behavior. Our tool uses genetic search to discover input transformations that induce systematic output differences aligned with an attacker-defined task, without modifying training data, architecture, or weights. We verify our approach against two targets. First, we target a MNIST digits classifier that we coerce into implementing a binary letter-recognition task. Then, we attack a production-grade NSFW classifier using face-specific perturbations to turn it into a proxy for demographic-group classification. In both cases, our method successfully enables the target backdoor. Finally, we discuss the existing countermeasures to assess the actual risk for the deployed systems.

nominations.title: Model-as-a-Trojan: Self-Activating Covert DNS Exfiltration Baked Into the Weights of an LLM Agent
nominations.authors: Barak Haryati, Shaked Zychlinski
nominations.abstract: Open-weight models are downloaded from public hubs and run inside agent harnesses that grant them tools, most powerfully, a shell, under the assumption that a sandbox contains whatever the model might do. This paper demonstrates that the assumption has a blind spot: the weights themselves can be the malware, and the sandbox's last open door, DNS, is enough. We fine-tune an open-weight LLM so that a single covert behavior lives in its parameters: on the first turn of every conversation, whenever the model infers from its context that a shell tool is available, it emits one self-contained command that reads a secret from the runtime environment, base32-encodes it, chunks it, and exfiltrates it as DNS queries toward an attacker-controlled authoritative name server. It then answers the user normally and never mentions, or repeats, the act. Because the channel is DNS, the attack completes from inside a container with no internet egress beyond name resolution - measured payload-level and model-level behind an egress firewall that drops every non-DNS packet, with the secret reconstructed from the gateway resolver's query log. Because the behavior lives in the weights, prompting is the only off-switch a victim has, and it is unreliable: the implant fires in 20/20 of adversarial suppression trials, deflects direct interrogation without disclosing the sequence, and sweeps a 45-cell sandbox-fault matrix across five tool-calling formats - plus a fresh post-training canary, persona-only and absent system prompts, and an egress-locked topology - with zero leaks and zero repeat fires. Every training trajectory is execution-verified in a real container, and every claimed exfiltration is proven resolver-side: we reconstruct the secret from the authoritative resolver's query log alone.

nominations.title: Can SOLARBURST go silicon? A systematic analysis on software supply chain attacks for VLSI design flows
nominations.authors: Fabiha Hashmat, Zeren Li, Santiago Torres-Arias
nominations.abstract: An attacker targeting the software supply chain (SWSC) of VLSI tools can fully subvert the VLSI design pipeline through purely software level compromises. However, cur- rent literature on both SWSC and VLSI hardware security has not explored how software can be used to subvert the security of the VLSI design flow. In order to bridge this gap, this paper presents a systematic analysis of the vulnerable surface of VLSI from a SWSC standpoint. We carry this anal- ysis through three major activities. First, we did an empirical analysis of VLSI software suites, focusing on their software composition, security features, and tool interactions within the VLSI design flow. Second, we develop a VLSI-SWSC attack taxonomy model that links software supply chain at- tacks and their mechanisms to the VLSI attacks they enable, the design-flow stages they affect, and their resulting security outcomes, allowing us to identify 717 possible new attacks, including 60 high feasibility attacks supported by evidence collected in our empirical analysis. Third, we identify what possible security outcomes can be achieved by an attacker from these attacks and produce a comprehensive VLSI SWSC threat model. We evaluate the feasibility of the attacks identi- fied by our taxonomy across VLSI design stages and assess existing defenses to determine which attacks are mitigated and which remain unaddressed. In addition, we present case studies using a reference VLSI design flow consisting of open- source VLSI tools and highlight attacks identified through our taxonomy on the VLSI SWSC uniquely from a software perspective.

nominations.title: StratFL: Countering Covert Model Poisoning Attacks with Strategic Federated Learning
nominations.authors: Manoj Twarakavi, Venkata Sriram Siddhardh Nadendla
nominations.abstract: Advanced persistent threats (APTs) are a major concern in federated learning (FL) deployments in critical sectors such as healthcare, and finance. Traditional defense mechanisms fail to contain APTs due to their intermittent attacking behavior. This paper addresses a specific type of APT called covert model poisoning (CMP) where the attacker intermittently injects poisoned model updates in a covert manner. The interaction between the FL server and a CMP attacker is modeled as an imperfect repeated game where both players cannot observe each other's actions. A novel adversarial search algorithm called StratFL is designed alongside novel belief update algorithms at both the server and adversary. Experiments are designed using MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets to evaluate and compare StratFL's performance against state-of-the-art methods. Empirical convergence of belief update algorithms is demonstrated across various security vignettes. At the same time, StratFL is found to exhibit an improved accuracy of 10% compared to state-of-the-art methods.

nominations.title: Exploring The Empirical Privacy Landscape of Synthetic Data
nominations.authors: Zihao Zhao, Avi Schwarzschild, Casey Meehan, Katherine Lee, Zhili Feng, Dylan Sam
nominations.abstract: Methods for training language models on sensitive data differ in how they balance capability gains against the risk of leaking private information. In this paper, we present a controlled comparison of data-level and training-level interventions for navigating the capability-privacy tradeoff on synthetic medical records with canaries to probe for leakage. Direct finetuning performs best on capability metrics but leads to the most privacy leakage, while DP-SGD reduces leakage at substantial cost to capabilities. Generating synthetic data from these records offers a more favorable balance, particularly when guided by a uniqueness-aware instruction to replace private details. Relative to naive paraphrasing, privacy-aware rewriting improves privacy protection across a variety of different rewriting models. We also find that more capable rewriting models generally reduce the risks of downstream privacy leakage, although held-out fit does not improve monotonically and increased test-time compute yields inconsistent gains. Overall, these results highlight privacy-aware rewriting as a promising direction for achieving a more favorable trade-off between capabilities and empirical privacy compared to other training-level methods, and our evaluation framework supports comparisons of future models and methods.

nominations.title: What It Is, Not What It Says: Securing Agentic Browsing Interactions with Web Semantics
nominations.authors: Umar Iqbal
nominations.abstract: AI agents increasingly browse the web on users' behalf, yet they consume webpages as screenshots or text, exposing their LLMs to unvetted third-party content. Browsers enforce semantics under which what an element can do depends on what it is and where it comes from, not on what it says. Agents flatten these semantics, so injected text can persuade the LLM to exercise the user's authority for content that has none. As LLMs remain easy to persuade, the agent's interface to the web must itself ensure the integrity of what the agent reads, interprets, and does. We propose Intact, which runs on an unmodified browser. Intact builds GenTree, a bespoke representation that captures provenance and web semantics. Intact passes the page via GenTree to the LLM one element at a time, so the LLM decides on each element without any other element's text. Its harness executes each step only within the capabilities of the step's element and asks the user before acting on third-party content. On 1,270 real webpages, GenTree attributes 2.3x as many elements to third parties as the browser, which misattributes 58.7% of them to the first party. On 1,091 of these webpages with injected attacks, only 12.8% of attacks get through Intact's planner, each at most as a consent request, against 73.1% for a conventional planner. Isolation disrupts functionality on only 3.7% of tasks, and a parallel schedule could remove most of its added latency.

nominations.title: ACE: An AI-Orchestrated Intrusion Detection and Compliance Mapping Engine
nominations.authors: Abdoulie Ceesay, Rishikesh Sahay, Md Rasel Al Mamun, Bell Raj Eapen
nominations.abstract: This study proposes the Automated Compliance Engine (ACE), an AI-orchestrated framework that links intrusion detection, regulatory control mapping, and automated countermeasure deployment for security operations environments. ACE integrates Suricata IDS, a LangGraph five-stage workflow, retrieval-augmented generation, NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control retrieval, large language model-based control ranking, and SSH-based Suricata rule deployment. The framework was evaluated in a two-virtual-machine laboratory using eight simulated attack scenarios and three legitimate traffic tests. ACE processed all eight attack alerts, achieved 100% alert detection, 0% false positives across legitimate traffic tests, generated deployable AUTO rules for 37.5% of alerts, verified 100% deployment of generated rules, and achieved an average NIST control-mapping confidence score of 0.87. The DeepEval assessment produced 1.0 scores for answer relevancy and faithfulness, while the hallucination score reflected known LLM-as-judge calibration limitations. The evaluation was conducted in a controlled environment with a limited attack set. Further validation is required using enterprise-scale telemetry, multiple IDS sensors, and an analyst-in-the-loop review. The results demonstrate how AI-assisted security automation can reduce analyst effort in translating IDS alerts into compliance-relevant evidence and defensive actions. ACE contributes an integrated detection-to-compliance-to-response workflow combining IDS telemetry, RAG-based control mapping, and automated rule deployment.

nominations.title: The LLM-Attacker: A Unified Red-Team Framework for Privacy Evaluation of Split and Distributed LLM Systems
nominations.authors: Georgios Politis, Evangelos Pappas
nominations.abstract: Split language models keep input text on a client but send intermediate representations to a server. Attacks can reconstruct text from these messages. Comparing privacy evaluations is difficult when attackers see different messages, know different model weights or use different datasets and recovery measures. We present LLM-Attacker, a framework that records these choices and lets researchers check, compare and extend an evaluation. Compatible attacks reuse recorded messages, and their predictions are saved for independent scoring. The scoring rule requires a linked undefended reference before a defence can pass. Reports also identify attacks that remain untested. In a controlled GPT-2 experiment, adding gradients returned during training increased token recovery from 94.20% to 97.38% and exact-document recovery from 13.71% to 37.77%. The 95% interval for the token gain lay above the two-percentage-point threshold fixed before testing. This experiment is shared with a companion study; here, it tests how the evaluation responds to a change in attacker access. Further studies measure how corpus choice and compression defences affect recovery, compare an adapted published attack with its reference implementation, and test the measurement code. The framework reports implementation checks separately from measured attack effectiveness. Each privacy claim should state the attacker, dataset and scoring rule, report its controls and identify untested attacks.

nominations.title: Veil-Then-Reveal: Protecting PII Privacy via Reversible Pseudo-Anonymization in Zero-Trust User--LLM Interaction
nominations.authors: Mohamed Shaaban, Mohamed Elmahallawy, Thomas E. Carroll
nominations.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly process sensitive documents and personal information, yet sending prompts containing personally identifiable information (PII) to remote providers exposes data subjects and organizations to risks from logging, retention, model training, and unintended disclosure. Existing anonymization methods often mask or remove PII, while conventional encryption eliminates the lexical and structural cues needed for effective LLM processing. We present Veil-then-Reveal (VtR), a user-side PII pseudo-anonymization framework for privacy-preserving LLM interaction under a zero-trust threat model. VtR treats remote LLM providers as untrusted and sends only pseudo-anonymized prompts, keeping plaintext PII on the user. VtR first detects PII and replaces it with realistic, same-type, in-vocabulary surrogates before prompts leave the user's device, preserving their linguistic and structural properties. It combines format-preserving encryption (FPE) for structured PII, such as phone and credit-card numbers, with a keyed-hash dictionary and secure vault for semantic PII, such as names, locations, and organizations. Session-specific mappings provide cross-session unlinkability, while user-side restoration reversibly replaces surrogates with their original values in LLM responses. We further introduce a rank-class FPE strategy for dates that preserves format and ambiguity while reducing cipher evaluations. Evaluation on three datasets containing 11,322 annotated PII instances achieves 97.9% detection recall, 95.2% protection of detected values, and 99.9% round trip; 100% of echoed surrogates end-to-end round-trip restoration.

nominations.title: GRAD: Graph-Structured Antibody Defense for LLM Agents
nominations.authors: Tianqi Song, Jiawei Du, Xuemei Jia, Zheng Wang
nominations.abstract: Memory poisoning and decomposition attacks distribute malicious evidence across the operations of large language model agents. Existing request-level defenses can miss such attacks because they assess individual inputs without connecting earlier information to later actions. Moreover, detectors must adapt as task contexts change, while updates to shared parameters can impair previously learned detection capabilities. To address these challenges, we propose GRAD, which combines graph-based evidence aggregation across operations with an extensible collection of detection experts. Its Semantic-Structural Understanding Module (SSUM) jointly encodes operation text, event attributes, and typed candidate relations in an execution graph to aggregate distributed attack evidence into a graph-level risk score. Its Continual Antibody Adaptation (CAA) adds experts on frozen encoder snapshots and routes inputs by observable graph signatures, acquiring and reusing detection capabilities as tasks arrive. Across Decomp, MCP, and MRT, GRAD achieves AUROCs of 97.19%, 77.59%, and 86.60%, respectively, outperforming Sequential Monitor and locally adapted Agent-Sentry and NeuroTaint. CAA improves final accuracy by 13.08 percentage points over Replay on the cross-dataset task stream. The gain remains 9.05 points with equal family/base-case weights within each task. Its compact drop-in gate performs local model inference in milliseconds without monitoring API calls.

nominations.title: Stealthy Poisoning Attacks via Reused KV Cache of Reasoning
nominations.authors: L. Zhu, Y. Jung, S. Szyller
nominations.abstract: Modern large language model (LLM) systems reuse key-value (KV) caches to accelerate inference. Recent work has shown that reusing KV caches from reasoning traces can also improve task performance, similar to retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). We demonstrate that this form of KV cache reuse introduces new poisoning vulnerabilities. We propose R$^2$ECAP (Reused Reasoning-Cache Poisoning), a black-box attack that plants poisoned reasoning traces solely through interactions with a system's chat interface. R$^2$ECAP constructs two traces: a preceding trace that steers the model toward an adversarial target and a retained trace that carries this target. Because the retained trace is generated conditioned on the preceding trace, its KV cache preserves residual adversarial influence, even after the preceding trace and its cache entries are discarded. We evaluate R$^2$ECAP on three open-weight LLMs and three datasets. R$^2$ECAP achieves up to 79% attack success rate (ASR) and outperforms HijackKV, a state-of-the-art white-box KV poisoning attack, in 8 of 9 resource-constrained settings. It also achieves 46% ASR in a realistic reasoning-trace retrieval system. Finally, R$^2$ECAP remains stealthy, with only 1% of its retained responses detected by a popular prompt injection detector.

nominations.title: RAMP: Toward Ubiquitous Quantum-Safe Key Distribution as a Service
nominations.authors: Jiafan Wang, Sebastian Kish, Dongxi Liu
nominations.abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) offers a security foundation independent of computational hardness assumptions. However, its reliance on specialized hardware limits access by ordinary users. Turning QKD into a service poses a fundamental trust challenge, as the providers that supply QKD-derived material themselves could retain knowledge of the keying inputs of users. This makes end-to-end confidentiality solely depend on the trustworthiness of the service infrastructure. We present RAMP, a service-oriented framework that decouples QKD material generation from key consumption. Providers operate QKD infrastructure and supply raw-key materials, while users securely acquire, mask, and locally process them into final keys without operating QKD devices. RAMP employs reconciliation-preserving masking compatible with both DV- and CV-QKD. It mitigates the trust dependence by separating the QKD-service and user-side masking domains. We formalize complementary confidentiality guarantees: RAMP protects the final key even if colluding providers expose their complete raw-key views, provided the masking domain remains secure; conversely, exposing the complete masking state does not break final-key secrecy as long as the QKD source and acquisition paths remain protected. The results establish the dual-domain security boundary of RAMP. We implement RAMP using experimentally acquired QKD data and standardized quantum-safe cryptography. After acquiring service-provisioned keying material, commodity endpoints complete user-side QKD post-processing with an average key-distillation throughput of 2.1Kb/s on an M4 Pro CPU. To our knowledge, we demonstrate the first experimental realization of such service-provisioned, user-side QKD processing, presenting a viable path toward QKD as a service.

nominations.title: Provable Authority: A Protocol for Verifiable Authority Resolution and Control Across Human, Organizational, and Agentic Transactions
nominations.authors: Jeremy Blackburn, Tim Hines, Matthew Koepp, Russell Lessard, Jason Patrick
nominations.abstract: Payment systems authenticate users, devices, accounts, and cryptographic credentials, but a relying party, such as a counterparty, payment rail, marketplace, or autonomous agent runtime, generally cannot obtain compact, independently verifiable evidence that the party presenting one exact transaction holds current organizational authority to execute it under the applicable evidence, policy, budget, and approval state. Agentic commerce makes this gap operationally urgent: a software agent can produce a valid signature while acting outside its delegated purpose, after its sponsor's authority has changed, or on transaction details that differ from those a human approved. We describe the ChainIT Authority Protocol, a subject-neutral and rail-neutral pre-execution authority and evidence control plane. The protocol separates durable identity, a versioned organizational authority record (the Authority Resolution Pactvera), sourced evidence assertions, deterministic reason-coded policy predicates, and organization-configured dispositions; binds each decision and human approval to a canonical transaction digest; reserves capacity atomically so that limits hold under concurrency; and authorizes commit only through a single-use, sender-constrained Execution Authorization Credential consumed at the rail adapter, with append-only lifecycle evidence sealed after the terminal outcome. An Agent Subject Profile adds the workload registration, attested key hierarchy, and sovereignty boundary required when the acting subject is an AI agent, without introducing a separate authority concept. We specify the commit-time execution predicate and bounded-freshness status rules, give enforcement profiles for fiat (ACH, wire, card, instant payment) and stablecoin rails, and state residual risks and non-goals.

nominations.title: Provable Compliance: A Protocol for Runtime Compliance Evidence and Transaction-Specific Decisioning
nominations.authors: Jeremy Blackburn, Tim Hines, Matthew Koepp, Russell Lessard, Jason Patrick
nominations.abstract: Regulated institutions already perform onboarding, screening, monitoring, and review, but compliance evidence ages, and whether it supports a decision depends on the institution, product, subject, counterparty, transaction, jurisdiction, risk tier, and purpose. A relying party therefore often cannot obtain compact, attributable proof of which evidence, policy, authority, and transaction context were current when a decision was made, a gap that grows as authority is delegated to software agents and scheduled workflows. We describe ChainIT Provable Compliance, the compliance-side layer of the ChainIT Authority Protocol. Each sourced or institution-generated fact is represented as a separate Evidence Assertion VDT with provenance, freshness, confidence, permitted purpose, and privacy classification; a versioned Compliance Policy Profile selects the applicable rules; a Business Rules Engine returns deterministic, reason-coded predicate results; and the organization's configured Workflow Engine composes them into a signed, time-bounded Compliance Decision VDT for one reliance event. The decision contributes a single predicate, Compliance Decision Permits, to session-eligibility and transaction-policy decisions. It never independently authorizes payment: only a final Allow together with an exact transaction digest, atomic capacity reservation, and a single-use execution credential can commit value. The paper specifies point-of-reliance freshness, scoped propagation of evidence changes, decision states, evidence domains (AML, sanctions, PEP, background, identity, and licensing), the U.S. and FATF regulatory context as of August 2026, privacy and disclosure controls, and residual risks.

nominations.title: When Core-Network Elements Become Reachable: Field-Level Exploitability Analysis in Diameter
nominations.authors: Wei Yi, Changlong Han, Xue Zhang, Qiao Zhang, Yi Chen, Jin Cao, Di Tang, Yulong Fu, Ben Niu, Hui Li
nominations.abstract: The increasing exposure of cellular core-network elements to public networks has turned Diameter signaling interfaces into a practical attack surface. While large language models (LLMs) show promise for protocol exploitability analysis, we find that their judgments on Diameter can be unreliable because they may deviate from the tacit analysis discipline followed by security experts and reach conclusions without considering complete protocol evidence. To address this challenge, we present LENS, an LLM-based system for reliable field-level Diameter exploitability analysis. LENS guides LLMs using both exploitability-analysis discipline and the protocol evidence needed for analysis. It infers analysis discipline from existing exploit writeups and evidence-collection guidance from exploitability-analysis failures, enabling systematic evidence collection, exploitability assessment, and proof-of-concept (PoC) attack generation when applicable. Our experiments show that LENS performs reliable analysis across four LLMs and repeated runs, achieving mean recall of 94.00% to 98.00%, precision of 78.73% to 88.94%, and accuracy of 84.00% to 92.00%. We find that more than 25% of field paths in the S6a and Cx interfaces are exploitable under the considered threat model. We further assess their impact on practical implementations and uncover 95 previously unknown vulnerabilities, including 17 in open-source EPC/IMS implementations and 78 in commercial deployments, causing service disruption, information leakage, subscriber tracking, and accelerated battery depletion. Applying LENS to 16 additional protocols spanning cellular, network, industrial, and host-internal systems uncovers 118 previously unknown vulnerabilities, demonstrating its strong generalizability.

nominations.title: SAFE-Mem: Secure Agentic Memory with Fine-Grained Authority and Governance-Aware Retrieval
nominations.authors: Haoming Li, Dingyi Kang, Xu Hu, Jinxin Yang, Zhu Xu, Chenru Wang, Yi Ge, Miao Yin, Guanpeng Li, Feng Chen, Bingzhe Li
nominations.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on persistent memory to support long-term reasoning and personalized interactions. However, information collected from external sources can introduce security risks when untrusted claims (i.e., atomic statements) are later treated as authorized preferences, policies, or permissions. Existing defenses typically rely on content-based filtering or coarse-grained provenance tracking, which either fail to prevent unauthorized memory use or block legitimate information, sacrificing memory utility. To address these limitations, we propose SAFE-Mem, a fine-grained memory governance framework that improves security while preserving legitimate memory use. First, SAFE-Mem annotates each claim with three governance labels (i.e., kind, authority, and scope) to capture its provenance and permitted use. Second, governance-aware retrieval matches query requirements with claim permissions to block unauthorized influence while retaining legitimate information. Third, a governance-enabled memory graph connects source sentences, claims, and entities to support provenance tracking and efficient retrieval. Across four LLM backbones on MPBench and LoCoMo, SAFE-Mem attains the lowest attack success among defenses that retain legitimate memory, at least 77% below the strongest of them, and the highest answer accuracy of all evaluated defenses, improving it by up to 15%. The code is available at https://github.com/LVenum/SAFE-Mem.
